name: security-gcp-cloudrun-invoker-review
intent: Cloud Run invoker identity, audience and application resource authority
artifacts: Service ingress/IAM, ID-token audience validation, proxy identity handling and handler policy.
trace: Resolve which layer authenticates invokers and which maps them to application tenants/resources. Keep public service admission separate from sensitive handler authorization.
experiment: Use an owned service fixture and synthetic response; compare intended invoker/audience with another owned principal or audience.
disproof: A public URL or a platform 403 alone does not prove handler exposure or correct object authorization.
repair: Align service admission and handler identity/resource checks, preserving expected service-to-service invocation.
branch_decisions: Distinguish service invoker IAM admission from application-level account/object checks. Verify the identity token audience expected by the configured service/custom audience and the actual ingress path. A publicly invokable service may be deliberate; the decisive issue is an unintended principal reaching protected application behavior, not the absence of an authentication prompt.
operational_method: Record whether the invoker IAM check is disabled or whether allUsers has an invoker grant; these are different publication configurations. Identify which Authorization or X-Serverless-Authorization header the platform validates and what identity the application then verifies. In a supplied trace, separate platform admission from handler resource access. A public service intentionally returning public content remains the control; do not infer application authentication solely from the platform header being present.
